entity.label: The thing observed (a price node, a balancing authority, a plant, a country, a station)
entity.rule: Written namespace:native_id, where the namespace is the publisher part of the table name and native_id is the publisher's own identifier, unchanged (ercot:HB_NORTH). Stable across tables, so tables can be joined on it.
entity.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

variable.label: What was measured (a price, a load, a count), in snake_case
variable.rule: Each table's file lists the values its variable column takes, with the unit of each.
variable.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

ts_utc.label: The time of the observation, in UTC
ts_utc.rule: ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z (2026-09-01T05:00:00Z). For an interval it marks the start of the interval. For a daily or longer frequency it is the date at 00:00:00Z and names the date the publisher reports (a trading date, a month, a year), not an instant.
ts_utc.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

value.label: The number observed, in the row's unit
value.rule: Never empty. A missing observation is an omitted row, not a row with an empty value. Nothing is interpolated, imputed or filled; a derived value is its own variable.
value.missing: Never empty; a missing observation has no row.

unit.label: The unit of the row's value
unit.rule: A word of the closed vocabulary of the data standard (MW, MWh, USD/MWh, pct, count and the others it lists), enforced by the validator.
unit.missing: Never empty in a series table; the validator requires it.

freq.label: How long the interval of the row is
freq.rule: An ISO 8601 duration (PT5M five minutes, PT15M, PT1H an hour, P1D a day, P1M a month, P3M a quarter, P1Y a year).
freq.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

geo.label: Where the thing is, as an ISO 3166-2 code (US-TX)
geo.rule: The smallest region that contains the entity. Where no single code applies, a comma-separated list with no spaces (US-CT,US-MA,US-ME). Checked by the validator.
geo.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

market.label: The market the value belongs to, lowercase (ercot_dam, ercot_rtm)
market.rule: The market or program within the publisher, as the table's file says.
market.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

node.label: The pricing node, hub or zone, written exactly as the publisher writes it (HB_NORTH)
node.rule: The publisher's own name for the price location, unchanged.
node.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

source.label: The publisher and its report or product, as organization:report_id (ercot:NP4-190-CD)
source.rule: Names the report the row was read from. For a table the ERW computes, erw:<builder>.
source.missing: Never empty; the validator requires it.

source_url.label: The address of the exact document the row was read from
source_url.rule: The document's own address, or the report page where the document has no stable address.
source_url.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

retrieved_at.label: When the ERW fetched the document, in UTC
retrieved_at.rule: ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.
retrieved_at.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

vintage.label: When the publisher published the document the value came from, in UTC
vintage.rule: Distinguishes revisions of the same observation. Where a table keeps more than one revision on purpose, vintage is part of its key.
vintage.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

ba.label: The balancing authority (the grid operator of an area) in EIA's code, lowercase (ciso, erco, us48)
ba.rule: The EIA-930 balancing authority code, lowercase, as the table name used to carry it before tables were joined (session 29).
ba.missing: Never empty in a table partitioned by it.

year.label: The operating year a history table was published by
year.rule: The publisher's year (for ERCOT, the year in Central time). Not derivable from ts_utc, whose first hours of 1 January UTC belong to the year before.
year.missing: Never empty in a table partitioned by it.

entity_id.label: The identifier of the thing, as namespace:native_id
entity_id.rule: The same rule as the series entity. Unique within the table.
entity_id.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

entity_type.label: What kind of thing the row is (plant, generator, project, datacenter, utility, company and the others the standard lists)
entity_type.rule: A word of the standard's list of entity types.
entity_type.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

name.label: The thing's name, as the publisher writes it
name.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

lat.label: Latitude, in decimal degrees (WGS84)
lat.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

lon.label: Longitude, in decimal degrees (WGS84)
lon.rule: WGS84 decimal degrees, east positive (so the United States is negative).
lon.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

capacity_mw.label: Nameplate capacity, in megawatts, as the publisher states it
capacity_mw.rule: The rating the publisher states; each table's file says which rating where its source says.
capacity_mw.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

status.label: The thing's state in the ERW's own words (operating, planned, under_construction, retired, withdrawn, active, completed, suspended)
status.rule: In an entities table, one of the eight words of Decision 20; the publisher's own status is kept in a column of its own. In an events table, the state of the deal or filing (announced, signed, approved, terminated and so on).
status.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

status_date.label: The date the status took effect, or was reported where the effective date is unknown
status_date.rule: YYYY-MM-DD. Each table's file says which of the two dates it is, where its source says.
status_date.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

operator.label: The operator or owner, as the publisher writes it
operator.rule: The publisher's name, or an entity_id where the operator is itself in an entities table.
operator.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

event_id.label: The identifier of the event, as namespace:native_id or a stable hash the connector documents
event_id.rule: The publisher's id (a docket number) where it has one; otherwise a stable hash documented by the connector. Unique within the table.
event_id.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

event_date.label: The date the event happened or was announced (each table's file says which)
event_date.rule: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ where the time matters (a story's publication time).
event_date.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

event_type.label: What kind of event the row is (ppa, interconnection_request, filing, announcement, acquisition, financing and others)
event_type.rule: A short snake_case word; each table's file lists the values it takes.
event_type.missing: Never empty; the standard requires it.

parties.label: The parties to the event, as the publisher names them, separated by semicolons
parties.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

entity_ids.label: The entity_id values of the things involved, separated by semicolons
entity_ids.rule: Values of an entities table's entity_id, joined by ";".
entity_ids.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

mw.label: The capacity involved, in megawatts
mw.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

price.label: The price, in the row's currency per MWh unless the table's file says otherwise
price.unit: the row's currency per MWh, unless the table's file says otherwise
price.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

currency.label: The currency of the price, as an ISO 4217 code (USD)
currency.missing: An empty cell means not given (the standard uses empty cells, never a code such as -999); the table's file says what that means there.

Imports: net_import_share_pct, net_import_days_pct, peak_import_share_pct, pair_import_share_pct (net_import_share_pct is EIA's balance, demand less net generation; the others are from the pair sums over complete days). Positive means the neighbour supplied the balancing authority (a net import). Pair rows (entity eia930:<BA>-<NEIGHBOUR>, x_to_ba the neighbour): net_import_mwh, net_import_share_pct, neighbor_report_mwh, neighbor_report_days. Partner rows: entity eia930:<BA>-<partner> from the authority's side (x_ba, x_partner). exchange_gross_mwh: the sum of the absolute hourly flows with x_partner by the authority's own report; net_import_mwh: the same flows signed, positive when it received power; x_rank_gross and x_rank_net rank its partners within the year (net by size, whichever direction); x_hours the hours it reported. net_import_share_of_demand_pct: its total interchange with the sign turned, summed over the hours it holds both that and its demand, over its demand in the same hours, percent (below zero: a net exporter); entity eia930:<BA>. Method: docs/methods/interchange_pairs.md.

"This is initial and final report." Event During backloading operations, the handrail of a gangway contacted a suspended 550-gallon tote tank of engine oil. Event Description - Sequence / Timeline On February 8, 2023, backloading operations were underway utilizing Drill side crane of the EI 314 A Facility. . At approximately 08:00HRS; the marine vessel (M/V) Wildcat transitioned from EI 314 A Production side, under crane, to the Drill side crane. . During the transition the rigger attached the hook of the Drill side crane to a full 550-gallon tote tank of engine oil. . The crane operator then hoisted the tote tank and positioned it over the water awaiting the M/V to move into position to receive it. . While the load was held in position the M/V began to reverse toward the platform and under the load. . Once in position to receive the load the M/V was exposed to side sea conditions which swayed the vessel up during side-to-side (transverse axis) movements. . At that time, the bottom of the tote tank encountered one of the handrails of a gangway. . As the boat leveled to its original elevation, the crane operator lifted the load slightly then swung the tote tank to the left, away from the gangway and then lowered the tote tank to the deck of the M/V. . Once backloading operations were complete the crane operator reported the event to the Person-in-Charge (PIC) on the platform and then the Field Foreman and AOL's incident reporting requirements were initiated which included reporting the incident to the Field Foreman, Production Forman, and HSE Coordinator for investigation. Event Consequences 1. Gangway handrail was bent downward, and a weld was broken on the base of a socket which connects the handrail to the walking plank. There were no environmental impacts, or injuries to personnel because of this event. Reference Final Report Attachment.

"This is the Initial and Final Report." Event Description - Sequence / Timeline On January 21, 2023, crane operations were underway utilizing the main crane located on the west of the EI 330 B Facility. At the time of the event, manifested materials were being offloaded from the marine vessel (M/V) on to the platform. . At approximately 18:50HRS; the M/V deckhand hooked the auxiliary line of the crane to a four-barrel drum rack (1,000 lbs.) that contained (4) empty DOT Drums and then provided a hoist hand signal to the crane operator. As the load was ascending, at approximately 1.5'- 4' FT off the back deck of the M/V, it contacted a tote tank and the securing binding chain of the tote tank. The binding chain and the sling assembly of a tote tank is where the initial load contact happened. As a result, the D-Style keeper pin inserted to secure the drum rack's door closed was damaged, failed, and the door opened. The drum rack's door then caught the interior railing of the M/V and (2) empty drums fell out of the drum rack. The crane operator and the boat captain conversed by radio and decided to continue with the lift, and the drum rack was offloaded and received on the platform. . The crane operator immediately reported the event to the Person-in-Charge (PIC) on the platform and then the Field Foreman and AOL's incident reporting requirements were initiated which included reporting the incident to the Field Foreman, Production Forman, and HSE Coordinator for investigation. Event Consequences 1. D-Style keeper pin was damaged resulting into failure. 2. Contents of the load became unsecured, and a portion fell to the deck of the M/V. 3. Barrel drum rack door hinge was damaged. There were no environmental impacts, or injuries to personnel because of this event.

eia861_net_metering.row: One utility's figure for its net-metered generators (capacity, customers or installations, energy sold back, or storage) by technology, in one state, balancing authority and customer sector, for one year, from Form EIA-861's net metering file.
eia861_net_metering.time: ts_utc is the data year's 1 January at 00:00:00Z (a year, not an instant); freq P1Y.
eia861_net_metering.vintage_rule: A run reads the years given with --years and writes the table whole; vintage is not filled. EIA's aggregates 88888 and 99999 left out; a '.' cell has no row.

source.name: eia:eia861:net_metering U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861 Annual Electric Power Industry Report (Net_Metering_<year>.xlsx)

eia861_net_metering.cite: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). Form EIA-861 Annual Electric Power Industry Report, net metering. Via the Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), table `eia861_net_metering`.
eia861_net_metering.header_title: EIA-861 net metering, each utility by state and sector, a year (session 869)
eia861_net_metering.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). entity eia861_nm:<utility>:<state>:<balancing authority>; variable EIA's headings joined (group and sector); unit MW, MWh or count as the heading names it; ts_utc the data year's 1 January; freq P1Y; node the utility's name; x_* EIA's fields.

eia930_demand_weather.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0), partition column ba; freq P1Y, ts_utc the first day of the local year. For each of energy (the mean of the year's hours), summer_peak (the highest hour of June to September), winter_peak (the highest hour of December of the year before to February) and overnight_min (the mean over the year's days of the lowest hour from midnight to 6 am, local): <figure>_mw metered, <figure>_expected_mw the fit's (the customers of 2019 to 2021 in that year's weather), <figure>_base_mw the mean of 2019 to 2021, <figure>_growth_pct, <figure>_weather_pct (the growth the weather explains), <figure>_unexplained_pct (growth minus weather; x_finding yes when it is larger than its uncertainty, beyond when the peak's hour was hotter or colder than any hour the fit was made on) and <figure>_uncertainty_pct (the largest miss of the years left out of the fit in turn; for a peak, never under the fit's error on one hour left out). <figure>_holdout_unexplained_pct on a row of 2019 to 2021: that year left out of the fit. fit_* on the row of 2019: the fit's hours and its mean absolute percent error.

10.2-mile 36-inch Line 31 loop parallel to existing Lines 14/18 plus a 1.6-mile 16-inch Line 14-P Lateral to Entergy Mississippi's planned Traceview Advanced Power Station, with a new Ridgeland Compressor Station (3 × 1,500 HP gas-driven units) and meter/regulator station  -  all in Madison County, MS. Adds 125,000 Dth/d of firm capacity. Application filed 1/23/2026 (CP26-75); total cost $131M. Construction planned 8/2027; target in-service 9/2028.

11/27/2024: VG Plaquemines rec'd FERC approval to place PH 1 facilities in service. Deliver feedgas to Plaquemines LNG via new interstate pipeline; interconnections with TGP (Southwest Lateral TGP) and TETCO.

12-mile lateral expansion of Energy Transfer's Tiger Pipeline, with capacity of up to 1 Bcf/d, to supply Entergy Louisiana's planned 2×750 MW Titanium Advanced Power Station in Richland Parish (serving Meta's hyperscale data center and the local grid). Supported by a 20-year firm transportation agreement starting with 250,000 MMBtu/d in February 2028 through January 2048, with an option for Entergy to expand capacity.

12-mile, 20-inch lateral from Dearborn County, IN through Boone County, KY to Hamilton County, OH. Serves Vistra Corp's Miami Fort coal-to-gas conversion (1,020-MW plant, June 2028 commercial operation). Vistra/Dynegy committed to full 265,000 Dth/d under 13-year contract. FERC authorization requested by March 19, 2027. Filed May 29, 2026.

ercot_storage_dam_offers_daily.header_shape:
Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0); freq P1D, ts_utc the operating day (local, Central) at 00:00:00Z; one entity, ercot:esr_fleet. A MWh here is a MW for an hour: of limit (limit_mwh and its parts: _out, _no_offer, _no_offer_out, _energy_offer, _as_offer, _award), of capacity offered or awarded, or of energy. Energy, from each resource's Energy Bid/Offer Curve: energy_offer_mwh (the most the curves offer to sell), energy_offer_mwh_le_

(what they offer at P USD per MWh or less, P in 0, 25, 50, 100, 250, 1000), energy_offer_mwh_at_clearing (at the hour's own day-ahead price at the resource's settlement point), energy_bid_mwh and energy_bid_mwh_at_clearing (the charging side), energy_sold_mwh and energy_bought_mwh (the awards). Ancillary Services (regup, regdn, rrs, ecrs, nspin), from the offer blocks: _offer_mwh, _offer_mwh_le_mcpc (priced at or below the hour's clearing price), _offer_mwh_le_

(P in 1, 5, 20, 100, 1000 USD per MW), _award_mwh, _award_usd, and _unawarded_usd (offered less awarded, each resource and hour, at the hour's clearing price). as_offer_mwh counts each block once; a block can be priced for several services. as_offer_mwh_unlisted: blocks offered by a resource with no row in ERCOT's ESR data file that hour, in no other sum. Counts: resources, resource_hours and its parts.

P1D rows (ts_utc the Pacific day at 00:00:00Z): alert_hours (count), alert_first_hour and alert_last_hour (local, the window's end), hours_assumed (1 where no notice gave hours: 16:00 to 21:00, else 0), basis_flex_alert (1 where the hours are the Flex Alert's, else 0; unit count), actual_mwh and predicted_mwh over the alert hours, reduction_mwh and reduction_mw (predicted less actual; positive is demand below the model) with _lo and _hi (90 percent interval), reduction_pct (of predicted), temp_max_f (population-weighted), train_days_as_hot (training days whose highest weighted temperature was at least the day's: the model's support), price_usd_mwh (mean day-ahead hub price over the alert hours), value_usd (reduction times price, summed) with _lo and _hi. flex_alert_model.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0), entity erw:flex_alert_model. Rows at ts_utc 2018-07-01T00:00:00Z (freq blank): pooled_<measure> (every alert hour of every alert day), oos_<metric> (the held-out hottest tenth of non-alert days, hours 16:00 to 21:00, five folds, each predicted by the model fitted on every other non-alert day: bias = mean of actual less predicted), pooled_reduction_mw_net_of_bias (the pooled reduction plus that bias), variant_<name>_<measure> (the five specifications compared: minimal, the prompt's CDH, CDH squared and the calendar; base, plus the 24 hours before and the dew point; base_prev24sq; base_cdh_dew; chosen, every term; robustness rows with 200 replicates), insample_<metric>, train_days, heldout_threshold_temp_f, alert_days_hotter_than_threshold, bootstrap_replicates, station_weight_<station>, coef_h<hour>_<term> (MW per unit of the term; the hour model's coefficients fitted on every non-alert day). P1D rows: heldout_error_mw (a held-out day's mean error in hours 16 to 20, actual less predicted), heldout_temp_max_f, heldout_price_usd_mwh.

generation_mix_records.cite: Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), derived. The energy mix by hour: the average day of each month and the records, from EIA-930 (docs/methods/generation_mix_hourly.md); The same for California from 2025-12-16, from CAISO's own supply by fuel (docs/methods/eia930_caiso_break.md). Via the Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), table `generation_mix_records`.
generation_mix_records.header_title: the energy mix's records by grid: the highest solar and wind shares of an hour, the cleanest and the dirtiest hour (session 94)
generation_mix_records.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). freq PT1H; ts_utc is the hour of the record (its start, UTC). Variables for the whole history, and with the prefix year_ for each local year (x_period: all, or the year). x_side: eia930 or caiso, the source of that hour. A share is of the hour's generation (the sum of what its sources put out; a source below zero adds nothing); the intensity is carbon_intensity_hourly's intensity_generation. Only held hours, and not an hour whose sources or whose CO2 do not describe it (docs/methods/generation_mix_hourly.md).

examples: A blank reason is kept blank ("local or system" is not guessed). The reason reaches back to 2022 in the interval table.
A day that is not whole is not written; March, August and September 2026 then have no monthly figure for California. Nothing is filled.
A day with a missing interval is not written. A twelve-month figure is written only when 95 percent of its hours are held, so ISO-NE's real-time figure in hub_price_comparison is not written.

A month's figures rest on the days held and say how many (days_held, days_left_out, thin_month). A figure that needs most of a year is not written under its share (SPP's carbon intensity in hub_price_comparison).

A pair-day is left out when it is further than 10 median absolute deviations, and at least 500 MWh, from the pair's own median over its history (warehouse/derived/ba_supply.py, MADS and FLOOR; the same rule in ai_power_regions.py and network_daily.py). The count left out is in each replay file and printed on the page.

examples: A day with a missing interval is not written. Session 65 recommended filling a single missing interval; the ERW's rule is to fill nothing, so it was not applied. Open for a ruling: the cost is ISO-NE's real-time twelve-month figure, which is not written.

A faulty hour of one balancing authority cannot be taken out of EIA's sum. The rule leaves out the one hour of the sum that fails it (2020-04-10T03:00Z), and the Lower 48 is given no peak. The Lower 48's consumed intensity of April 2020 goes with the held carbon build. It stays open until EIA republishes the hours or the ERW builds its own sum from the screened authorities, which no session has been asked to do.

A gap at the source: there is nothing for the ERW to fix, and nothing is filled. Each figure says how many days it rests on. Open because EIA has not been asked why SPP's days are missing, and a figure for SPP that rests on 200 of 365 days is a weak one however plainly it says so.
Both figures are shown as the report states them, with the note. Which is misstated only ERCOT can say; it has not been asked.
Both sides' reports are in the table side by side and the headline says which it uses. The disagreement is the publishers'.

By letter filed November 13, 2025, Grenfell, LLC, and Flat River Power, LLC, informed the Commission that the exemption from licensing for the Belding Dam Project No. 9379, originally issued March 17, 1986, has been transferred to Flat River Power, LLC. The project is located on the Flat River, Ionia County, Michigan. The transfer of an exemption does not require Commission approval.

1. By letter filed November 3, 2025, Kinneytown Hydro Company, Inc. and Connecticut Brownfield Land Bank, Inc. informed the Commission that the exemption from licensing for the Kinneytown Hydro Project No. 6985, originally issued May 20, 1983, has been transferred to Connecticut Brownfield Land Bank, Inc. The project is located on the Naugatuck River in Seymour, Connecticut. The transfer of an exemption does not require Commission approval.

1. Commission staff hereby protests pursuant to section 284.123(g)(4)(i) of the Commission's regulations, the compliance filing made by Consumers Energy Company (Consumers Energy) on February 2, 2026, in the above referenced docket. On May 19, 2025, as amended on September 12, 2025, Consumers Energy filed an application under section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (NGA) and section 284.224 of the Commission's regulations for a limited jurisdiction blanket certificate to transport and sell natural gas in interstate commerce and requested authority to use its state-approved Transmission only Transportation (TOT) service rate as the rate for service. In an order issued on December 18, 2025, the Commission directed Consumers Energy to revise its TOT service rate to comply with the Commission's rate design policies or provide a reasonable justification as to why it qualifies for an exemption.

1. Commission staff hereby protests, pursuant to section 284.123(g)(4)(i) of the Commission's regulations, the rate petition made by Bay Gas Storage Company, LLC (Bay Gas) on July 30, 2026, in the above referenced docket. Pursuant to sections 284.123(b)(2) and 284.123(g) of the Commission's regulations, Bay Gas filed a rate petition to revise rates for firm and interruptible interstate transportation services provided under section 311 of the Natural Gas Policy Act of 1978. Bay Gas states that the instant rate petition complies with its commitment to file a petition for rate approval on or before July 30, 2026, as stipulated in an amendment filing in Docket No. PR21-58-000. Bay Gas also states that in compliance with an agreement with Commission staff in Docket No. PR21- 58-000, it has incorporated Original Cost of plant into the cost of service for its proposed rates. Bay Gas argues that it qualifies for an exemption to the Commission's straight-fixed variable (SFV) rate design policy due to its long-standing rate design that was the result of a settlement in March 1999 which has been carried forward since without change.

1. In Order No. 901, the Commission directed the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), the Commission-certified Electric Reliability Organization (ERO), to develop new or modified Reliability Standards that address specific matters pertaining to the impacts of inverter-based resources (IBR) on the reliable operation of the Bulk-Power System. Due to the significant scope of the work, the Commission required NERC to submit responsive Reliability Standards in three tranches. On November 4, 2025, NERC submitted three petitions seeking approval of five proposed Reliability Standards and related definitions, representing the second tranche of Reliability Standards directed by the Commission in Order No. 901.

examples: A Cheniere company has asked DOE for a 25-year permit to export LNG to countries without a free trade agreement with the US, from a planned expansion of its Corpus Christi terminal in Texas. DOE is taking public comment until June 15, 2026 and has not decided.

A Louisiana LNG terminal has asked DOE for permission to export more natural gas to countries without a free trade agreement with the United States. The company says this needs no new construction, and DOE will take public comment until 2026-05-26.

A company called ST LNG has asked DOE for permission to export liquefied natural gas from a proposed offshore terminal near Matagorda, Texas, to countries without a free trade agreement with the United States. DOE is taking comments and protests until 2026-02-23 and has not made a decision.

A company has applied to the NRC for a license to build and run a uranium enrichment plant in Kentucky using laser technology. The NRC is reviewing it, will hold a required public hearing after its reviews, and is also letting interested people ask for a contested hearing.

A company has applied to the NRC for permission to build four reactors in Idaho that would make isotopes, not electricity. The NRC is still checking whether to accept the application, and no public participation steps have been set yet.

scripps_co2_mlo_monthly.cite: Scripps CO2 Program (Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego). Primary Mauna Loa CO2 Record: monthly in situ CO2. Via the Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), table `scripps_co2_mlo_monthly`.
scripps_co2_mlo_monthly.header_title: the Scripps CO2 Program (Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego), atmospheric CO2 at Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii, from in situ air measurements, a month from 1958 (session 2137)
scripps_co2_mlo_monthly.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). entity scripps:mlo; variables co2 (the monthly mean, adjusted to the 15th) and co2_seasonally_adjusted; unit ppm (Decision 67, micromoles per mole of dry air, the 2012 SIO manometric scale); ts_utc the month's first day; freq P1M; x_station MLO, or MKO (Maunakea's summit) for the months after Mauna Loa's 2022 eruption.

shoulder_hours_monthly.header_title: the shoulder hours, ERCOT and CAISO, by local month (sessions 75 and 80)
shoulder_hours_monthly.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). freq P1M; ts_utc is the first day of the local month at 00:00:00Z. The average day by local hour (avg_<demand|solar|wind|net_load|battery>_mw_hHH), the midday surplus, the evening shoulder and the battery fleet against it; definitions in docs/methods/shoulder_hours.md ("shoulder" is this table's term). Session 80: a second measure that ends inside the evening (shoulder2_*: net load above the midpoint between its daily mean and its evening peak); freq P1D, the ten days of each local year with the largest evening shoulder energy (worst_rank, day_*); freq P1Y, each year's means and its ten worst days (year_*).

statcan_energy_balance_annual.cite: Statistics Canada. Table 25-10-0029-01, Supply and demand of primary and secondary energy in terajoules, annual. Via the Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), table `statcan_energy_balance_annual`.
statcan_energy_balance_annual.header_title: Statistics Canada, table 25-10-0029-01, supply and demand of primary and secondary energy, by province and fuel, a year, 1995 to 2024 (session 2383)
statcan_energy_balance_annual.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). entity statcan_eb:<area>:<fuel>; variable the supply and demand line as a slug; unit MWh (StatCan's terajoules times 1,000,000/3,600); freq P1Y; ts_utc the year's 1 January; geo CA, CA-<province>, or blank for the Atlantic provinces (atl) and the three territories together (ter); x_fuel, x_line StatCan's names; x_vector; x_terminated t for an ended series. Fuels and lines overlap (totals hold their parts): a sum takes one level. Exports, stock variation (positive for a build) and transformation are subtracted; transfers and adjustments are signed and added; the statistical difference is not part of final demand. Electricity's demand lines, under primary electricity, cover all electricity; its statistical difference leaves out secondary net supply in 2005 to 2009. Primary electricity's production appears to hold wind, solar and tidal too (StatCan does not say).

PROHIBITION ON COST SHIFTING AND RECOVERY OF COSTS."] || curtailment or backup generation: curtailment of a commercial data center's load under regional transmission organization curtailment programs, and curtailment standards [p. 20, regulations (2): "(2) CURTAILMENT OF A COMMERCIAL DATA CENTER'S LOAD UNDER"]

commission rulemaking: A public utility serves a new large load only under a commission-approved service contract, filed with a no harm test; the commission approves or denies it within 270 days [p. 1, 61-335(2): "A public utility shall provide service to a new large load only pursuant to a commission-approved service contract." | p. 1, 61-335(3), (4): "Such filing shall include a no harm test ... The commission shall review and approve or deny a new large load service contract within two hundred seventy (270) days of receiving such filing by the public utility."] || cost allocation: The new large load funds its full cost of service, including its share of generation, transmission, substation and distribution investments needed only because of it; the commission reviews the contract's rates in each general rate case [p. 1, 61-335(4)(b): "The new large load is responsible for funding its full cost of service, including its share of generation, transmission, substation, and distribution infrastructure investments" | p. 1, 61-335(7)(a): "In each general rate case filed by a public utility, the commission shall review the rates, charges, and cost recovery mechanisms applicable to an approved service contract"] || collateral: Approval is conditioned on financial security, in a form and amount the commission approves, reasonably sufficient to protect the utility and its other customers from stranded or unrecoverable costs [p. 1, 61-335(6): "Approval of a service contract shall be conditioned on the new large load furnishing financial security, in a form and amount approved by the commission"] || other: A new large load may not change its status by artifice, such as splitting its load among service entrances [p. 1, 61-335(5): "A new large load shall not change its status as such by means of artifice"]

commission rulemaking: each investor-owned electric company and electric cooperative must submit a specific rate schedule for large load customers by 1 September 2026; the PSC must adopt regulations by 1 June 2026 on notice and deadlines for load studies and contract terminations, forms of collateral, and study completion [p. 17, PUA 4-212(c)(1): "SHALL SUBMIT TO THE COMMISSION FOR APPROVAL A SPECIFIC RATE SCHEDULE FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS." | p. 19, PUA 4-212(f)(1): "ADOPT REGULATIONS TO CARRY OUT THIS SECTION." | p. 19, PUA 4-212(f)(2)(ii): "COMMON FORMS OF ACCEPTABLE COLLATERAL TO SATISFY THE REQUIREMENTS OF"] || minimum bill: in approving a schedule the PSC must consider minimum billing demand for distribution and transmission at a high percentage of contract capacity, long-term commitments and exit fees, guarantee or collateral requirements, and penalties if a project is delayed or cancelled after buildout begins [p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(ii): "AND TRANSMISSION SERVICE THAT IS A HIGH PERCENTAGE OF A LARGE LOAD" | p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iii): "(III) LONG-TERM CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS AND EXIT FEES;" | p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iv): "(IV) GUARANTEE OR COLLATERAL REQUIREMENTS; AND"] || cost allocation: the schedule should require the customer to cover the just and reasonable costs of transmission or distribution buildout to interconnect or serve it, payable over multiple years of the contract not exceeding 5 years [p. 18, PUA 4-212(e): "THE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY ELECTRIC TRANSMISSION OR DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM BUILDOUT REQUIRED UNDER SUBSECTION (D)(1) OF THIS SECTION MAY BE PAID OVER MULTIPLE YEARS OF A LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER'S CONTRACT FOR SERVICE, NOT TO EXCEED 5 YEARS."] || interconnection study: before signing a contract under the schedule the customer must request a load study to set its contract capacity and pay its fees, designate a site, and own or control the land [p. 19, PUA 4-212: "NECESSARY CONTRACT CAPACITY FOR THE LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER AND PAY ANY" | p. 19, PUA 4-212: "APPLICABLE FEES ASSOCIATED WITH THE STUDY;"]

commission rulemaking: the BPU must set standards by order for every electric public utility within 12 months; each utility must then petition for a large data center rate class and tariff [p. 1, Section 1b: "No later than 12 months after the effective date of this section, the Board of Public Utilities shall establish, by order for every electric public utility, standards for the provision of electricity to large data center customers by electric public utilities." | p. 1, Section 1c: "each electric public utility shall file a petition with the board for approval of a rate class and tariff for the provision of electricity to large data center customers."] || minimum bill: adequate financial guarantees to pay for at least 85 percent of the electricity supply requested, for 10 years from when service commences, unless the BPU's standards say otherwise [p. 1, Section 1d(1): "data center customer provides adequate financial guarantees that it will pay for at least 85 percent of the ... it requests for a period of 10 years from when service commences or as otherwise determined in the board"] || collateral: deposits, financial security or, for customers with sufficiently high credit ratings, financial commitments, in forms the BPU approves, over the 10-year period [p. 1, Section 1d(2): "provide for the posting of deposits, financial security, or, for ... center customers with sufficiently high credit ratings, financial commitments, in respective forms approved by the board"] || exit fee: no exit fee printed; the BPU may approve a stranded cost recovery mechanism applicable only to the large data center class [p. 1, Section 1d(2): "authorize the board to approve a stranded cost recovery mechanism applicable exclusively to the large data center customer class"] || interconnection study: new large data center customers pay the reasonable costs of interconnection, system impact and facilities studies [p. 1, Section 1d(8): "require any new large data center customer to ... pay the reasonable costs of any interconnection, system impact, and facilities"] || curtailment or backup generation: priority curtailment of large data center customers before residential customers in system emergencies, as firm load shed; demand flexibility commitments [p. 1, Section 1b(11): "ensure the priority curtailment of large data ... center customers before residential customers, excluding designated critical" | p. 1, Section 1d(5): "(5) require demand flexibility commitments by large"]

commission rulemaking: the Commission must establish by order, by 15 December 2026, the definition and characteristics of a very large customer class or subclass for each public utility, in a rate case or another proceeding; it may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement between a utility and a very large customer [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 1: "The commission may do this in a rate case under section 216B.16 for that utility or in another proceeding." | p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2: "The commission may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement proposed between a public utility and a very large customer establishing the terms and conditions under which the utility will provide electric service to the customer."] || cost allocation: the Commission must consider how best to achieve that all costs attributable to very large customers not exempt are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(1): "(1) all costs attributable to the utility's very large customers not exempt under subdivision 3 are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass determined by the commission under paragraph (a);"] || exit fee: no exit fee printed: the tariff or agreement must contain protections so other customers are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs of serving the very large customer [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(3): "(3) the tariff or agreement contains protections necessary to ensure that other customers of the public utility are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs associated with the utility serving the very large customer; and"] || other: the electricity provided to a very large customer must achieve each benchmark of the state's electricity standards (216B.1691), shown by a utility plan to serve the load without asking to delay or modify the standards; existing, renewed or extended agreements and very large customers taking service before 2020 are exempt [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(2): "(2) the electricity to be provided by the utility to a very large customer achieves each quantitative benchmark of the state's electricity standards under section 216B.1691" | p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 3: "This section shall not apply to existing, renewed, or extended electric service agreements of public utility customers meeting the threshold of a very large customer, or to very large customers that have been actively taking electric service from the public utility prior to 2020."] || other: an annual fee the commissioner collects from each qualified large-scale data center, by the peak demand the utility arranges to serve: 2,000,000 dollars for 100 to 250 MW up to 5,000,000 dollars for 750 MW or more, paid into the energy and conservation account [p. 1, 216B.72(a): "(a) The commissioner must collect an annual fee from the qualified large-scale data center, on a schedule prescribed by the commissioner and deposited in the energy and conservation account established in section 216B.241, subdivision 2a." | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(1): "$2,000,000" | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(4): "(4) 750 MW or greater" | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(4): "$5,000,000"] || other: each public utility must offer an optional clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers by special contract, with participants paying all proportional costs of the new resources and no cost shifting either way [p. 1, Sec. 10, 216B.1623: "The commission shall require each public utility to offer a clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers." | p. 1, 216B.1623(5): "(5) prohibit cost shifting from the participating customers to other utility customers or vice versa; and"]

examples: A 2024-session act approved 17 January 2025 and in effect in 2025. It sets terms for data centers' electric service as conditions of a sales and use tax exemption, not as a utility rule. The companion Act No. 208 of 2024 (Enrolled H.B. 5600, effective 2 April 2025) was opened but not read for terms. No 2025 or 2026 Michigan act on large loads was found (one web search; a Michigan moratorium bill is a news lead only).

Amends PUA 4-212 (from Chapter 625 of 2025) and adds Part III, 7-232 to 7-234; it keeps the 1 September 2026 rate schedule filing date (4-212(c)(1)(i), p.34). Dataset row pjm_east-03 (proposed COMAR 20.96.01, RM 93) cites this chapter for its threshold. Effective date: the chapter has several effective-date sections (July 1, 2026 for listed sections; the rest from enactment as an emergency measure); which section carries these provisions was not traced, so not published here. Existing large load customers whose load does not expand by more than 25 MW are outside the schedule (4-212(c)(2)(iii)).

Coordinator's lead (a Governor's release: HB 233 signed 26 August 2026) confirmed on the General Assembly's bill page: House Substitute 1 for HB 233, Signed 8/26/26, Volume:Chapter 85:440, Effective Date 8/26/26. The text read is the engrossment of HS 1 as amended (House Amendments 1 and 3, Senate Amendment 2). The bill page's synopsis says rate applications are due within 180 days of the effective date; the engrossed Section 6 says within 180 days of the finalization of the Commission's regulations, and the engrossed text is quoted. No dataset statewide row exists for Delaware (Delmarva's tariff is Exelon's, whose site terms bar automated access).

Found through the Code of Virginia's 2026 Updates list for Title 56 (law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodeupdates/title56/). The bill numbers behind chapters 377 and 378 and their approval dates were not read: the LIS bill pages (lis.virginia.gov) are built by script and the legacy LIS has no 2026 session; the Code page prints the year only, so status_date is '2026' and the effective date is not printed. The prompt's lead, S.B. 503 of 2026, was not confirmed. The 2026 uncodified acts list names chapter 591 (HB 323, waste heat from data centers, a work group) and other utility items, none setting large-load terms. Code of Virginia 56-585.1 as published carries no data center or large-load term and no 2025 or 2026 chapter in its history line, so no 2025 Virginia act is entered. The Virginia SCC host is paused and was not asked. status_date as the reading group wrote it: '2026'.

Introduced bill; only the introduced version is posted, with six House floor amendments filed (H-8203 to H-8214). The bill history is not rendered in the page read, so no later action is stated; Iowa's 2026 session has ended. Leads not read: SF 2249 and HF 2261 (large energy use facilities of 20 MW or more), from trackers only.

statsmu_mauritius_electricity_annual.cite: Statistics Mauritius. Economic and Social Indicators, Energy and Water Statistics (2023 and 2025 editions), Tables 1, 7 and 8. Via the Energy Research Warehouse (ERW), table `statsmu_mauritius_electricity_annual`.
statsmu_mauritius_electricity_annual.header_title: Statistics Mauritius, Energy and Water Statistics, electricity generation by source, capacity, peak demand and sales, 2017 to 2025 (session 2409)
statsmu_mauritius_electricity_annual.header_shape: Shape: series (docs/datastandard.md v0). entity statsmu:MU (the Republic of Mauritius); ts_utc the year's 1 January; freq P1Y; geo MU. From Table 1: generation_total, renewable_share (pct), electricity_sold (MWh). From Table 7: capacity_installed, capacity_effective, peak_demand_mauritius, peak_demand_rodrigues (MW). From Table 8: generation_hydro, _wind, _landfill_gas, _photovoltaic, _gas_turbine_kerosene, _fuel_oil_diesel, _coal, _bagasse (the 2025 edition's "Bagasse & Fuelwood"), generation_renewable (MWh, the tables' GWh times 1,000). Tables 7 and 8 give each edition's two years only (2022 to 2025); Table 1 gives 2017 to 2025. Generation is every producer's, the independent producers' own use included; electricity_sold is the CEB's sales, so generation less sales is not losses. Capacity includes plants not exporting to the CEB (Table 7's footnote); effective capacity is not defined.

AEP Texas's own tariff (aeptexas.com, Tariff for Electric Delivery Service effective 5 January 2026) answered HTTP 404 and was not read; no AEP Texas large-load schedule is named in the 10-Q (AEP's pending Texas large-load tariff is SWEPCo-Texas, outside ERCOT). The 10-Q: in August 2026 the Governor directed a verification of Batch Zero loads and an audit of data center projects 25 MW and above; ERCOT 'has currently paused Batch Zero classification and study activity and stated it will not authorize large loads to energize until verification is complete.' Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-21): exit_fee was '16 TAC §25.194: 20% of the security for allocated capacity kept on withdrawal before the SLLIA deadline, 20% of the security for withdrawn contracted demand kept after a SLLIA, security forfeited without a SLLIA; CIAC not refundable (statewide row)'. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-23): collateral now names the guaranty and the letter of credit the rule accepts.
